questions.prompt: The storm was approaching. The crew covered the instruments. They hoped to keep them dry. Which sentence uses because for the cause and an infinitive for the purpose?
choices: Because the storm was approaching, the crew covered the instruments to keep them dry.
Although the storm was approaching, the crew covered the instruments and hoped to keep them dry.
The crew covered the instruments because the storm was approaching and to keep them dry.
So the storm was approaching, the crew covered the instruments to keep them dry.
questions.explanation: Because introduces the approaching storm as the reason for covering the instruments, and to keep them dry states the purpose with an infinitive phrase.
questions.topic: Combine Three Sentences - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Combine: A fox crossed the yard. It carried a wicker basket. The basket held three eggs. Which sentence combines all three facts with an introductory participial phrase?
choices: Crossing the yard, a fox carried a wicker basket, and the basket held three eggs.
A fox crossing the yard carried a wicker basket, and the basket held three eggs.
A fox, crossing the yard, carried a wicker basket, and the basket held three eggs.
A fox crossed the yard carrying a wicker basket, and the basket held three eggs.
questions.explanation: The introductory participial phrase Crossing the yard correctly modifies the subject a fox, while the two coordinated clauses preserve all three facts.

questions.prompt: Combine: The match continued. Rain fell throughout the game. The players completed the final drill. Which version uses regardless of correctly to show that the rain did not stop the match?
choices: Regardless to the rain, the match continued, and the players completed the final drill.
Despite of the rain, the match continued, and the players completed the final drill.
Regardless of the rain, the match continued, and the players completed the final drill.
Regardless of raining, the match continued, and the players completed the final drill.
questions.explanation: Regardless of is correctly followed by the noun the rain, and the phrase shows that the match continued despite the weather.
questions.skill: Using the Concessive Phrase Regardless Of

questions.prompt: The fork in the trail was muddy. We could take the bridge. We could follow the ridge. Which sentence uses although for the initial detail and coordinates parallel verbs with either...or?
choices: Although the fork in the trail was muddy, we could either take the bridge or we could follow the ridge.
Although the fork in the trail was muddy, we could either take the bridge or follow the ridge.
Although the fork in the trail was muddy, we could either take the bridge or following the ridge.
Although the fork in the trail was muddy, we could either taking the bridge or follow the ridge.
questions.explanation: The either...or construction coordinates the parallel bare infinitives take the bridge and follow the ridge after the introductory although clause.
questions.skill: Combining clauses with although and either...or

questions.prompt: The morning rehearsal ended early. The evening rehearsal began on time. The directors approved the revised schedule. Which combination is fully grammatical and uses whereas to contrast the rehearsals while preserving all three actions in the simple past?
choices: The morning rehearsal ending early, whereas the evening rehearsal began on time, and the directors approved the revised schedule.
The morning rehearsal ended early, whereas the evening rehearsal began on time, the directors approved the revised schedule.
The morning rehearsal ended early, whereas the evening rehearsal began on time, and the directors were approving the revised schedule.
The morning rehearsal ended early, whereas the evening rehearsal began on time, and the directors approved the revised schedule.
questions.explanation: Whereas contrasts the two independent clauses about the rehearsals, and the final coordinated clause states that the directors approved the revised schedule.
questions.skill: Combining three sentences with whereas and coordinated clauses

questions.prompt: Combine: A volunteer guided the visitors. The visitors were new to the museum. She answered their questions. Which version combines all three facts while keeping the volunteer as the subject of both main-clause verbs?
choices: The volunteer guided the visitors, who were new to the museum, and answered their questions.
The volunteer guided the visitors who were new to the museum and answered their questions.
The volunteer, who was new to the museum, guided the visitors and answered their questions.
The volunteer guided the visitors, who were new to the museum, and they answered their questions.
questions.explanation: The correct option uses a nonrestrictive relative clause to identify the visitors while keeping the volunteer as the subject of both guided and answered.

questions.prompt: The volunteers arrived early. They unpacked many boxes. They hoped to finish by noon. Which sentence combines all three facts and correctly uses an infinitive phrase to express purpose?

The volunteers arrived early and unpacked many boxes for finish by noon.
The volunteers arrived early and unpacked many boxes to finished by noon.
The volunteers to arrive early unpacked many boxes to finish by noon.
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase to finish by noon expresses the volunteers' purpose and is introduced by the preposition to followed by the base verb finish.

questions.prompt: A technician labeled each cable. The students followed the labels. They completed the setup safely. Which sentence correctly uses so that to express the purpose of the labels?
choices: The technician labeled each cable so that the students could follow the labels and complete the setup safely.
Because the technician labeled each cable, the students followed the labels and completed the setup safely.
The technician labeled each cable so the students followed the labels and completed the setup safely.
The technician labeled each cable unless the students followed the labels and completed the setup safely.
questions.explanation: The so that clause explains that the labeling was intended to help the students follow the instructions and complete the setup safely.

questions.prompt: Combine: The power failed unexpectedly. The hallway lights flickered. Students guided one another with flashlights. Which version correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause and a while clause?
choices: After the power failed unexpectedly the hallway lights flickered while students guided one another with flashlights.
After the power failed unexpectedly, the hallway lights flickered while students guided one another with flashlights.
After, the power failed unexpectedly, the hallway lights flickered while students guided one another with flashlights.
After the power failed unexpectedly, the hallway lights flickered while, students guided one another with flashlights.
questions.explanation: The introductory dependent clause After the power failed unexpectedly is followed by a comma, and the while clause correctly shows the students guiding one another as the lights flickered.

questions.prompt: The whistle blew. The runner left the starting line. The crowd began cheering. Which version correctly uses not until with subject-auxiliary inversion while preserving all three facts?
choices: Not until the whistle blew did the runner leave the starting line, and the crowd began cheering.
Not until the whistle blowing did the runner leave the starting line, and the crowd began cheering.
Not until the whistle blew the runner leave the starting line, and the crowd began cheering.
Not until the whistle did blow the runner leave the starting line, and the crowd began cheering.
questions.explanation: The construction Not until the whistle blew did the runner leave the starting line correctly places did before the subject, while and adds the crowd's action.
questions.skill: Subject-auxiliary inversion after a negative adverbial

questions.prompt: Combine: Three people entered the museum. One carried a map. The others asked for directions. Which combination introduces the two details with a colon and then coordinates them with a comma and and?

Three people entered the museum: one carried a map, and the others asked for directions.
Three people entered the museum: one carried a map, and the others asked directions.

questions.prompt: A coach called the volunteers. The volunteers were new. She thanked them. Which sentence correctly uses whom to combine all three facts?

The coach called the new volunteers, who she thanked.
The coach called the new volunteers, whom they thanked.
The coach called the new volunteers, which she thanked.
questions.explanation: Whom is the object of both called and thanked because it refers to the volunteers, whom the coach called and then thanked.

questions.prompt: The whistle sounded. The runners immediately lined up. They entered the track. Which sentence uses as soon as to show that lining up followed the whistle immediately?
choices: As soon as the whistle sounded, the runners lined up and entered the track.
When the whistle sounded, the runners lined up and entered the track.
Because the whistle sounded, the runners lined up and entered the track.
Although the whistle sounded, the runners lined up and entered the track.

questions.prompt: Combine: Ms. Ortiz is the team captain. She arrived early. She greeted us at the door. Which version correctly sets off the appositive and forms a compound predicate without an unnecessary comma before and?
choices: Ms. Ortiz the team captain, arrived early and greeted us at the door.
Ms. Ortiz, the team captain arrived early and greeted us at the door.
Ms. Ortiz, the team captain, arrived early, and greeted us at the door.
Ms. Ortiz, the team captain, arrived early and greeted us at the door.

questions.prompt: The final results were impressive. The team completed every task. Every judge praised its accuracy. Which sentence correctly uses a colon to introduce the two supporting details?
choices: The final results were impressive: the team had completed every task, and every judge praised its accuracy.
The final results were impressive, the team had completed every task, and every judge praised its accuracy.
The final results were impressive; the team had completed every task, and every judge praised its accuracy.
The final results were impressive: the team had completed every task; and every judge praised its accuracy.
questions.explanation: The colon correctly introduces the details that support the statement about the final results, and and joins the two independent clauses within that explanation.

questions.prompt: Combine: The tent shook in the wind. Everyone ducked. The lantern fell over. Which version combines all three facts by using an absolute construction?
choices: With the tent shaking in the wind, everyone ducked as the lantern fell over.
After the tent shook in the wind, everyone ducked when the lantern fell over.
During the tent shaking in the wind, everyone ducked, and the lantern fell over.
The tent was shaking in the wind, so everyone ducked while the lantern fell over.
questions.explanation: The correct option begins with the absolute construction With the tent shaking in the wind before joining the remaining two actions in the main clause.

questions.prompt: Visitors must wait outside when the garden gate is closed. They may enter the garden when the gate is open. Which sentence correctly expresses the condition with unless?
choices: Visitors must wait outside unless the garden gate is open, in which case they may enter the garden.
Visitors may enter the garden unless the garden gate is closed, and they must wait outside when it is open.
Visitors must wait outside unless the garden gate is open, but they may enter the garden when it is closed.
Visitors must wait outside because the garden gate is open, and they may enter the garden when it closes.
questions.explanation: Unless the gate is open, visitors must wait outside, and the in which case clause explains that they may enter once it is open.

questions.prompt: A bakery displayed a new mural. A local artist designed it. Customers stopped to photograph it. Which sentence uses a past participial phrase to identify the mural's creator?
choices: A bakery displayed a new mural designing by a local artist, and customers stopped to photograph it.
A bakery displayed a new mural design by a local artist, and customers stopped to photograph it.
A bakery displayed a new mural designed by a local artist, and customers stopped to photograph it.
A bakery displayed a new mural designed a local artist, and customers stopped to photograph it.

questions.prompt: The practice test was difficult. The final exam was equally difficult. The students studied carefully for both. Which sentence combines all three facts and correctly uses as...as?
choices: The final exam was as difficult as the practice test, and the students studied carefully for both.
The final exam was as difficult so the practice test, and the students studied carefully for both.
The final exam was more difficult as the practice test, and the students studied carefully for both.
The final exam was as difficult than the practice test, and the students studied carefully for both.

questions.prompt: We could have taken the bus. Instead, we walked home. The lighter traffic gave us time to talk. Which sentence correctly pairs rather than with a gerund and punctuates the introductory phrase?

Rather than taking the bus we walked home, and the lighter traffic gave us time to talk.
Rather than take the bus, we walked home, and the lighter traffic gave us time to talk.
Rather than to take the bus, we walked home, and the lighter traffic gave us time to talk.
questions.explanation: This version correctly pairs rather than with the gerund taking and properly sets off the introductory phrase.

questions.prompt: Combine: The sensor detected smoke. The alarm sounded. The hallway filled quickly. Which version most clearly presents the smoke detection as the cause of the two later events?

Since the sensor detected smoke, the alarm sounded, and the hallway filled quickly.
When the sensor detected smoke, the alarm sounded, and the hallway filled quickly.
If the sensor detected smoke, the alarm sounded, and the hallway filled quickly.

The rain was so heavy that stream flooded the path, so we turned back.

questions.prompt: Combine: The hike was exhausting. The group kept moving. They reached the summit before noon. Which version uses despite with a gerund phrase and sets it off correctly with commas?
choices: Despite of the hike being exhausting, the group kept moving and reached the summit before noon.
Despite the hike being exhausting the group kept moving and reached the summit before noon.
Despite the hike being exhausting, the group kept moving and reached the summit before noon.
Despite the hike was exhausting, the group kept moving and reached the summit before noon.

questions.prompt: Combine: Emi brought no camera. She brought no tripod. She still planned to photograph the eclipse. Which version uses neither...nor correctly and expresses the contrast with yet?
choices: Emi brought neither a camera nor a tripod, yet she still planned to photograph the eclipse.
Emi brought neither a camera or a tripod, yet she still planned to photograph the eclipse.
Emi brought neither camera nor tripod, yet she still planned to photograph the eclipse.
Emi brought neither a camera nor a tripod, so she still planned to photograph the eclipse.

questions.prompt: Combine: The roads froze. The buses were delayed. Many students arrived late. Which version uses because to express the first cause and so to express the resulting effect?

Because the roads froze the buses were delayed, so many students arrived late.
Because the roads froze, the buses were delayed, so many students arrived late.
Because the roads froze, the buses were delayed so many students arrived late.

questions.prompt: The aquarium added a new exhibit. It displays tools from ancient trade routes. Visitors can explore a replica ship. Which combination correctly uses a nonrestrictive relative clause to include all three facts?

The aquarium added a new exhibit which displays tools from ancient trade routes, and visitors can explore a replica ship.

The aquarium added a new exhibit, displays tools from ancient trade routes, and visitors can explore a replica ship.

questions.prompt: Combine: The club will plant trees. It will install benches. It will create a garden. Which sentence uses three parallel predicates?

questions.prompt: The robotics workshop has two activity stations. At one station, participants build a small robot. At the other, they program a drone. Which sentence combines all three facts and correctly uses either...or?

questions.prompt: The gate opened. The judges entered. The spectators took their seats. Which version correctly punctuates an introductory dependent clause before two coordinated independent clauses?

questions.prompt: The first dataset was incomplete. The second dataset was larger. The researcher repeated the experiment. Which option combines the facts, uses so to express a result, and gives the two research actions as a parallel active compound predicate?
